Special Attacks: Improved grab, swallow whole

Special Qualities: Low-light vision, scent

Imported from the d20 SRD; verify attacks and skills in-game. Full rules at d20srd.org.

system.biography:
Despite its enormous size and 6-ton weight, a tyrannosaurus is a swift runner. Its head is nearly 6 feet long, and its teeth are from 3 to 6 inches in length. It is slightly more than 30 feet long from nose to tail.

Combat

A tyrannosaurus pursues and eats just about anything it sees. Its tactics are simple—charge in and bite.

Improved Grab (Ex)

To use this ability, a tyrannosaurus must hit an opponent of up to one size smaller with its bite attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and can try to swallow the foe the following round.

Swallow Whole (Ex)

A tyrannosaurus can try to swallow a grabbed opponent of up to two sizes smaller by making a successful grapple check. The swallowed creature takes 2d8+8 points of bludgeoning damage and 8 points of acid damage per round from the tyrannosaurus’s gizzard. A swallowed creature can cut its way out by using a light slashing or piercing weapon to deal 25 points of damage to the gizzard (AC 12). Once the creature exits, muscular action closes the hole; another swallowed opponent must cut its own way out.

A Huge tyrannosaurus’s gizzard can hold 2 Medium, 8 Small, 32 Tiny, or 128 Diminutive or smaller opponents.

Skills

A tyrannosaurus has a +2 racial bonus on Listen and Spot checks.

system.benefit: You get a +2 bonus on all Listen checks and Spot checks.

When running, you move five times your normal speed (if wearing medium, light, or no armor and carrying no more than a medium load) or four times your speed (if wearing heavy armor or carrying a heavy load). If you make a jump after a running start (see the Jump skill description), you gain a +4 bonus on your Jump check. While running, you retain your Dexterity bonus to AC.

You gain +3 hit points. For every Hit Die beyond 3, you gain an additional +1 hit point. If you have more than 3 Hit Dice, you gain +1 hit points whenever you gain a Hit Die (such as when you gain a level).

system.description: You can follow the trails of creatures and characters across most types of terrain.
system.benefit: To find tracks or to follow them for 1 hour requires a Survival check. You must make another Survival check every hour to continue following the tracks. The DC depends on the surface and the prevailing conditions.
system.special: A ranger automatically gains Track as a bonus feat at 1st level. He need not select it.

system.description: Your Listen check is either made against a DC that reflects how quiet the noise is that you might hear, or it is opposed by the target's Move Silently check.
Your Spot check is either made against a DC that reflects how obvious the object is, or it is opposed by the target's Hide check.

What it does (SRD): In starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar dim lighting, the creature can see twice as far as a human can in the same light. It retains the ability to distinguish color and detail under those conditions that a human could not.

ThirdEra: Low-light vision is set on this item’s Details tab under Capability grants (vision and senses), not in Mechanical effects (no extra distance is needed for the usual reading of the rule). The character sheet includes it with other vision from items and race.

What it does (SRD): Scent lets the creature detect opponents by smell, usually out to about 30 ft. (strong scents farther, very weak scents closer). It can use scent to pinpoint a square once it is within 5 ft., and to track by Survival. Wind and water affect what it can smell.

ThirdEra: Scent (30 ft.) is set on this item’s Details tab under Capability grants (vision and senses), not in Mechanical effects. The character sheet includes it with other senses; Survival checks to track by scent still use the normal skill rules unless you add separate bonuses elsewhere.

What it does (SRD): If the creature hits with a listed natural weapon, it can attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking attacks of opportunity. Details (size modifiers, opposed checks, holding vs pinning) follow the grapple rules.

ThirdEra: This template has no numeric rows in Mechanical effects or Capability grants. Track grapple state in play; use the NPC’s natural attacks and CMB/CMD from the sheet when resolving the grapple.

What it does (SRD): If the creature starts its turn with an opponent grappled in its mouth, it can swallow that opponent with another successful grapple check. Swallowed creatures can attack from inside, may be affected by acid or bludgeoning damage from the gizzard, and escape by cutting free or escaping the grapple.

ThirdEra: This item is prose-first: keep Mechanical effects and Capability grants empty unless you add a homebrew numeric row. Use the printed bite/gizzard damage, AC to cut out, and interior space from the stat block.
